svg.title: Ishikari metro map, readable

g.title: Ishikari metro map: How to read this map. Click for more.
g.text: Read it clockwise, from Task at the top.

g.title: Part 1: 1 ASK · 2 PLAN Click for more.
Part 2: 3 BUILD · 4 CHECK · 5 FIX · 6 MERGE Click for more.
Part 3: 6 FINISH: JUDGE · MAIN MOVES Click for more.
Plan line: The first stretch of the ring: from your task to the specs and worker plans. Click for more.
Question line: The investigator asks you, you answer. Click for more.
Research line: The investigator sends researcher ants. Click for more.
Build line: The long stretch of the ring: build, check, merge, judge, finish. Click for more.
Many-plan rail: 2+ plans: one worker ant and one detective ant per plan. Click for more.
Fix loop: A bug goes back to the worker and is re-checked. Click for more.
Fix loop, many plans: A bug goes from the Detective ants back to the Worker ants. Click for more.
Clash line: Tasks that break together go back to the fix loop. Click for more.
Dropped spur: A task that could not be fixed leaves here. Click for more.
Merge failed spur: A failed merge goes back to the worker ants. Click for more.
Cleanup failed spur: A failed cleanup becomes a suggested next task. Click for more.
Jury rail: 3+ merged tasks: one juror ant per task. Click for more.
Judge fix loop: Below 7 with gaps, or 7+ with bugs: one fix round. Click for more.
After main moves: Green: the run's work is on main. Click for more.
Check failed spur: A failed app check starts one new task. Click for more.
Fast path: A trivial task skips the planning and build ants: straight across the ring to MAIN. Click for more.
Merge failed spur: merge failed: to Worker ant s6 Click for more.
g.text: merge failed: to Worker ant s6

g.title: Junction: Where the dropped spur leaves the line. Click for more.
Dropped spur: dropped Click for more.
Cleanup failed spur: cleanup failed: to Task s1 (next run) Click for more.
g.text: cleanup failed: to Task s1 (next run)

g.title: Check failed spur: check failed: to Worker ant s6 (new task) Click for more.
g.text: check failed: to Worker ant s6 (new task)

g.title: Fast path: fast path: to MAIN s18 Click for more.
Junction: Where the judge fix loop rejoins the line. Click for more.
Junction: Where the clash line rejoins the line. Click for more.
Task (s1): The work you hand Ishikari. Click for more.
Investigator ant (s2): Asks you questions, then writes the two specs and every plan. Click for more.
You (s3): You answer the investigator's questions. Click for more.
Researcher ants (s4): Look up facts for the investigator. Click for more.
Specs + worker plans (s5): Everything the investigator writes: the product spec, the tech spec and one plan per worker. Click for more.
Worker ant (s6): Build the plans, one worktree each. Click for more.
Detective ant (s7): Check each built task and plan every fix. Click for more.
Integrator ant (s8): Merges all passing tasks in a scratch copy and tests once. Click for more.
Merger ant (s9): Merges the approved tasks for real, then checks with git; failures go back to the workers. Click for more.
Janitor ant (s10): Cleans up mess the run left, by itself. Click for more.
Juror ants (s11): Score each merged task against its plan. Click for more.
Judge ant (s12): Scores the whole run 0-10 against the product spec. Click for more.
Worker ant (s13): Closes the judge's gaps or bugs. Click for more.
Detective ant (s14): Checks the judge fix and lands it. Click for more.
Judge ant (s15): Scores again after the fix. Click for more.
Docs ant (s16): Updates the repo's docs for the merged tasks, or writes them from scratch, last, on the final code. Click for more.
Finisher ant (s17): Moves main, cleans up, runs the check. Click for more.
MAIN (s18): Your main branch, moved forward. Click for more.
checkCommand (s19): Builds and checks the app after main moves. Click for more.
Retrospective ant (s20): Reviews how this run went and suggests fixes to the Ishikari flow. Read only. Click for more.
Run report (s21): The run ends with one report. Click for more.
Logbook (s22): Every ant's reply, one entry each. Click for more.
Worker ants (s23): Build the plans, one worker ant per plan. Click for more.
Detective ants (s24): Check each built task and plan every fix, one detective ant per task. Click for more.
Junction: Where the many-plan fix loop meets the dropped spur. Click for more.
Decision: facts missing?: Decides whether any researcher ant runs. Click for more.
g.text: no: none · yes: rail, 1 to 5 at once

g.title: Decision: how many plans?: Decides how many worker and detective ants there are. Click for more.
g.text: 1: main line, one worker · 2+: rail, one per plan

g.title: Decision: --parallel <n>?: Decides whether worker, detective and juror ants run one at a time or together. Click for more.
g.text: no: one at a time · yes: up to n at once

g.title: Decision: 3+ merged tasks?: Decides whether juror ants run. Click for more.
g.text: no: main line, judge alone · yes: rail, one juror per task

svg.script: (function(){ var D=[{"y":550,"sub":[],"name":"Ishikari metro map","tip":"How to read this map.","src":"skills/ishikari/design/index.md","id":"title","code":"","x":850,"about":"Ishikari runs a task with many ants, one worker, detective or juror at a time unless you pass --parallel. The map is one open ring: read it clockwise from Task at the top, round to the Run report. The gap at the top says a run ends; the next one is yours to start. Loops and spurs bend inside the ring. Hexagons are ants (AI agents), diamonds are decisions, the ring is the single-ant path and a triple rail leaving it is a many-ant path, pages are files, dashed lines are side branches, and colour means something: green done, red failed, yellow warning. Click anything to learn what it is; Esc closes this panel."},{"y":642.7,"sub":[],"name":"Junction","tip":"Where the many-plan fix loop meets the dropped spur.","src":"","id":"junction-drop-rail","code":"","x":1186.7,"about":"Not a station: a task on the many-plan rail that cannot be fixed leaves its fix loop here too, down the same dropped spur as a task on the main line."},{"y":600,"sub":[],"name":"Key","tip":"What the cars, symbols and colours mean.","src":"","id":"key","code":"","x":670,"about":"Top: what each numbered car shows; the main line carries one car, each rail three small cars side by side, one per rail. Middle: the symbols: hexagon an ant, bin dropped, circle an interchange, diamond a decision about how many ants run or whether a stop is skipped, triple rail a lane where several ants run, leaving the single-ant main line at a decision and rejoining it, stacked hexagons a stop where several ants run (the mark ∥ after a name: always at once), dashed a side branch. Bottom: green done, red failed, yellow warning, blue plan, indigo build."},{"y":150,"sub":[],"name":"Part 1","tip":"1 ASK · 2 PLAN","src":"skills/ishikari/SKILL.md","id":"part-1","code":"","x":1670,"about":"Steps 1 and 2, the blue stretch from Task to the worker plans: the investigator asks you its questions, then writes the product spec, the tech spec and one plan per task; the plan stage only checks the plans. The only part where you are asked anything."},{"y":1280,"sub":[],"name":"Part 2","tip":"3 BUILD · 4 CHECK · 5 FIX · 6 MERGE","src":"skills/ishikari/SKILL.md","id":"part-2","code":"","x":1670,"about":"Steps 3 to 5 and the first half of step 6, the indigo stretch down the right and along the bottom: worker ants build the plans, one at a time or up to 5 at once with --parallel, detective ants check each one and plan fixes, the integrator tests all passing tasks together, then the merger lands them in a scratch copy and the janitor cleans up. Main has not moved yet."},{"y":1280,"sub":[],"name":"Part 3","tip":"6 FINISH: JUDGE · MAIN MOVES","src":"skills/ishikari/SKILL.md","id":"part-3","code":"","x":30,"about":"Step 6, second half, up the left side: the judge scores the run against the product spec, the docs ant updates the docs, the finisher moves main forward and runs the check, the retrospective ant reviews the run, and the run is reported."},{"y":303.6,"sub":[],"name":"Plan line","tip":"The first stretch of the ring: from your task to the specs and worker plans.","src":"","id":"line-plan","code":"","x":1197.9,"about":"The blue line carries one task from Task through the investigator and what it writes, the two specs and the worker plans, on to the worker ants, where building starts."},{"y":128.3,"sub":[],"name":"Question line","tip":"The investigator asks you, you answer.","src":"","id":"line-ask","code":"","x":1124.0,"about":"The investigator's questions go up to you and your answers come back as messages to the same live agent. The dot riding it is one round of questions."},{"y":376.2,"sub":[],"name":"Research line","tip":"The investigator sends researcher ants.","src":"","id":"line-res","code":"","x":1046.1,"about":"Up to 5 researcher ants at once look things up and report back down this line while the investigator waits. From the facts decision on it is a triple rail: several ants at once. The dot riding it is one burst of research."},{"y":1209.7,"sub":["a plan may run a saved workflow in place of a worker ant","built: its detective is next in line (--parallel: starts at once)","no gaps, or 7+ with no bugs: no fix round"],"name":"Build line","tip":"The long stretch of the ring: build, check, merge, judge, finish.","src":"","id":"line-g1","code":"","x":831.9,"about":"The indigo trunk carries every task from the worker ants through checking, the combined test, the merge, the cleanup and the judge to MAIN. It is the single-ant path: one worker ant, one detective ant, the judge alone. Where a run uses several ants a triple rail leaves it at a decision and rejoins it. The numbered cars on it are tasks."},{"y":653.4,"sub":[],"name":"Many-plan rail","tip":"2+ plans: one worker ant and one detective ant per plan.","src":"","id":"line-many","code":"","x":1268.4,"about":"A triple rail means several ants. With two or more plans the run leaves the main line at the plans decision: one worker ant per plan builds it, one detective ant per task checks it, one at a time or up to n at once with --parallel, and the rail rejoins at the integrator, which tests the passing tasks together. The rail has its own fix loop, from the Detective ants back to the Worker ants, and the clash line joins it. With one plan the run stays on the main line: one worker ant, one detective ant."},{"y":568.4,"sub":["bugs: the detective's fix plan goes back to the worker;","the worker builds it, the detective re-checks; 3 tries per bug"],"name":"Fix loop","tip":"A bug goes back to the worker and is re-checked.","src":"","id":"line-fix","code":"","x":1304.0,"about":"Yellow means a warning: the detective found a bug and planned its fix. The worker builds the fix and the detective re-checks, up to 3 tries per bug and 3 fix rounds."},{"y":648.6,"sub":["bugs: each task's detective sends its fix plan back to that task's worker;","3 tries per bug, 3 fix rounds"],"name":"Fix loop, many plans","tip":"A bug goes from the Detective ants back to the Worker ants.","src":"","id":"line-mfix","code":"","x":1187.5,"about":"Yellow means a warning. On the many-plan rail each task has its own loop: its detective ant finds a bug and plans the fix, that task's worker ant builds it, and the detective re-checks, up to 3 tries per bug and 3 fix rounds. One at a time by default, or several tasks at once with --parallel. A task that still has bugs leaves down the dropped spur."},{"y":711.8,"sub":["fail: tasks clash: the task takes them in, then the fix loop; 2 rounds"],"name":"Clash line","tip":"Tasks that break together go back to the fix loop.","src":"","id":"line-clash","code":"","x":1099.0,"about":"Only a run with two or more plans can clash, so this line joins the many-plan rail's fix loop. When the integrator's combined test shows two passing tasks clash, the task takes in the tasks it clashes with and goes back through that loop: its worker fixes it, its detective re-checks. 2 rounds at most."},{"y":652.4,"sub":[],"name":"Dropped spur","tip":"A task that could not be fixed leaves here.","src":"","id":"line-drop","code":"","x":1117.9,"about":"A task drops when a bug is still open after 3 tries, when 3 fix rounds end with bugs open (both: escalated), when its worker is blocked or hits an error, or when its after names a task that dropped: tasks built on it drop too. The main session drops it without asking; it never reaches finish or main and nothing sends it back. Its branch is kept for a later look, and the final report lists it with why it dropped, its bugs and fix history."},{"y":972.1,"sub":[],"name":"Merge failed spur","tip":"A failed merge goes back to the worker ants.","src":"","id":"line-mback","code":"","x":1174.5,"about":"A conflict, failed tests, or a task git cannot find goes back to the worker ant on its own branch: it merges main and fixes it, then the detective, integrator and merger run again. At most 2 extra build rounds."},{"y":1010.4,"sub":[],"name":"Cleanup failed spur","tip":"A failed cleanup becomes a suggested next task.","src":"","id":"line-tnext","code":"","x":1035.0,"about":"If the janitor's tests fail, main moves with the tasks alone, the cleanup branch is kept, and its note is offered as the Task of the next run."},{"y":1164.8,"sub":[],"name":"Jury rail","tip":"3+ merged tasks: one juror ant per task.","src":"","id":"line-jury","code":"","x":883.2,"about":"A triple rail means several ants. With 3 or more merged tasks the run leaves the main line at the jury decision: one juror ant per merged task scores its own task, one at a time or up to n at once with --parallel, and the rail rejoins at the judge ant. With 1 or 2 merged tasks the run stays on the main line and the judge works alone."},{"y":896.0,"sub":["below 7 and gaps: one fix round for every gap","7+ and bugs: one fix round for the bugs only","a failed fix keeps its branch; the verdict says why"],"name":"Judge fix loop","tip":"Below 7 with gaps, or 7+ with bugs: one fix round.","src":"","id":"line-jfix","code":"","x":507.1,"about":"Yellow means a warning: the judge scored the run below 7 and listed gaps, or passed it but listed bugs, gaps where the code behaves wrongly. A worker closes the gaps, or at 7 or more only the bugs, a detective checks and fast-forwards the fix, and the judge scores again. Only one round."},{"y":297.6,"sub":[],"name":"After main moves","tip":"Green: the run's work is on main.","src":"","id":"line-after","code":"","x":508.8,"about":"After MAIN moves the finisher runs the check, the retrospective ant reviews the run, and the main session reports it."},{"y":400.6,"sub":[],"name":"Check failed spur","tip":"A failed app check starts one new task.","src":"","id":"line-cfix","code":"","x":479.6,"about":"If checkCommand fails after main moved, one build round runs as a new task named check-fix, from the moved main. Still failing: the run stops."},{"y":520.7,"sub":[],"name":"Fast path","tip":"A trivial task skips the planning and build ants: straight across the ring to MAIN.","src":"","id":"line-fast","code":"","x":358.3,"about":"Once the product spec is written the investigator judges the task: trivial means a small, known scope (1-2 files), no design choice and one task; any question asked makes it not trivial. You confirm once. The main session then builds from the product spec alone: it edits on a branch in a worktree, runs the test and check commands, fast-forwards main only when both pass and logs it through ishikari.py. If it turns out bigger or a check keeps failing, the edits are thrown away and the full plan runs, told why."},{"y":972.1,"sub":["the worker merges main and fixes it;","max 2 extra build rounds"],"name":"Merge failed spur","tip":"merge failed: to Worker ant s6","src":"","id":"spur-mback","code":"","x":1174.5,"about":"A conflict, failed tests, or a task git cannot find goes back to the worker ant on its own branch: it merges main and fixes it, then the detective, integrator and merger run again. At most 2 extra build rounds."},{"y":625.1,"sub":[],"name":"Junction","tip":"Where the dropped spur leaves the line.","src":"","id":"junction-drop","code":"","x":1312.0,"about":"Not a station: the point where the dropped spur branches off. A task drops when a bug is still open after 3 tries, when 3 fix rounds end with bugs open (both: escalated), when its worker is blocked or hits an error, or when its after names a task that dropped: tasks built on it drop too. The main session drops it without asking; it never reaches finish or main and nothing sends it back. Its branch is kept for a later look, and the final report lists it with why it dropped, its bugs and fix history."},{"y":652.4,"sub":["after 3 tries on a bug or 3 fix rounds,","a blocked or failed worker, or a task","built on a dropped one; branch kept"],"name":"Dropped spur","tip":"dropped","src":"","id":"spur-drop","code":"","x":1117.9,"about":"A task drops when a bug is still open after 3 tries, when 3 fix rounds end with bugs open (both: escalated), when its worker is blocked or hits an error, or when its after names a task that dropped: tasks built on it drop too. The main session drops it without asking; it never reaches finish or main and nothing sends it back. Its branch is kept for a later look, and the final report lists it with why it dropped, its bugs and fix history."},{"y":1010.4,"sub":["branch kept; its note is offered"],"name":"Cleanup failed spur","tip":"cleanup failed: to Task s1 (next run)","src":"","id":"spur-tnext","code":"","x":1035.0,"about":"If the janitor's tests fail, main moves with the tasks alone, the cleanup branch is kept, and its note is offered as the Task of the next run."},{"y":400.6,"sub":["one build round from the moved main;","still failing: the run stops"],"name":"Check failed spur","tip":"check failed: to Worker ant s6 (new task)","src":"","id":"spur-cfix","code":"","x":479.6,"about":"If checkCommand fails after main moved, one build round runs as a new task named check-fix, from the moved main. Still failing: the run stops."},{"y":520.7,"sub":["trivial task, you confirm; the main session","edits, tests, checks and lands it"],"name":"Fast path","tip":"fast path: to MAIN s18","src":"","id":"spur-fast","code":"","x":358.3,"about":"Once the product spec is written the investigator judges the task: trivial means a small, known scope (1-2 files), no design choice and one task; any question asked makes it not trivial. You confirm once. The main session then builds from the product spec alone: it edits on a branch in a worktree, runs the test and check commands, fast-forwards main only when both pass and logs it through ishikari.py. If it turns out bigger or a check keeps failing, the edits are thrown away and the full plan runs, told why."},{"y":926.1,"sub":[],"name":"Junction","tip":"Where the judge fix loop rejoins the line.","src":"","id":"junction-jfix-end","code":"","x":386.7,"about":"Not a station: the point where the judge fix loop rejoins. Yellow means a warning: the judge scored the run below 7 and listed gaps, or passed it but listed bugs, gaps where the code behaves wrongly. A worker closes the gaps, or at 7 or more only the bugs, a detective checks and fast-forwards the fix, and the judge scores again. Only one round."},{"y":701.9,"sub":[],"name":"Junction","tip":"Where the clash line rejoins the line.","src":"","id":"junction-clash-end","code":"","x":1189.8,"about":"Not a station: the point where the clash line rejoins. Only a run with two or more plans can clash, so this line joins the many-plan rail's fix loop. When the integrator's combined test shows two passing tasks clash, the task takes in the tasks it clashes with and goes back through that loop: its worker fixes it, its detective re-checks. 2 rounds at most."},{"y":181.4,"sub":["you give it, or a","dropped cleanup plan"],"name":"Task","tip":"The work you hand Ishikari.","src":"SKILL.md#1-setup","id":"task","code":"s1","x":958.1,"about":"Your task in your own words, or the note of a cleanup the last run dropped. Setup makes the run's state folder and env first; the main checkout must be on the main branch with no uncommitted changes."},{"y":249.0,"sub":["one live agent on Opus at low effort: it asks you,","proves the task can be built, and writes the product","spec, the tech spec and every plan; no other ant plans"],"name":"Investigator ant","tip":"Asks you questions, then writes the two specs and every plan.","src":"skills/investigator-ant/SKILL.md, assets/prompts/investigator.md, SKILL.md#2a-investigate","id":"investigator","code":"s2","x":1125.6,"about":"One live agent run by the skill, not a workflow, on Opus at low effort, like every other ant. It loads the investigator-ant skill in its Ishikari mode, reads what the task needs and gets each answer as a message. Part 1: it critiques the task, finds the test command, asks up to 4 independent questions at a time, 8 in all, writes the product spec and judges whether the task is trivial. Part 2, when told to go on: it proves the task can be built, writes the tech spec and one plan per worker ant, and may ask you again when the design needs a choice. No other ant plans, so nothing is lost between ants. It stays alive until its plans pass the check or a fast path lands. Ishikari needs the Agent tool for it."},{"y":128.3,"sub":["up to 4 questions a round (/ask-simple),","8 in all; answering approves the whole run"],"name":"You","tip":"You answer the investigator's questions.","src":"SKILL.md#2a-investigate","id":"you","code":"s3","x":1124.0,"about":"The only time Ishikari asks you anything. Questions come through /ask-simple, up to 4 at a time, about 8 in all. Answering approves the whole run, merge to main included."},{"y":376.2,"sub":["up to 5 at once, web + computer,","read only; the investigator waits"],"name":"Researcher ants","tip":"Look up facts for the investigator.","src":"SKILL.md#limits","id":"researchers","code":"s4","x":1046.1,"about":"Up to 5 at once, with or without --parallel: they only read, so nothing can collide. On Opus at low effort. They search the web and the whole computer, read only, never secrets, and report back. The investigator starts them and waits for them. They are not logged."},{"y":369.9,"sub":["product_spec.md: behaviours B1... and invariants I1...;","tech_spec.md: the architecture and the code's shape;","one thin plan per worker (none for one worker), checked before anything is built"],"name":"Specs + worker plans","tip":"Everything the investigator writes: the product spec, the tech spec and one plan per worker.","src":"<state>/plans/<run>/product_spec.md, tech_spec.md, <task>.md","id":"specs","code":"s5","x":1259.8,"about":"All written by the investigator, in this order. product_spec.md, once nothing important is unclear: two lists and nothing else. Behaviours, what the product does once the task is done, each with an id (B1, B2...) and written as given / when / then; invariants, what must always hold, each with an id (I1, I2...). Every one is written so an ant can check it, and each answer you gave shows up as the behaviour it led to. A task that changes no behaviour has invariants only. Then the trivial verdict: a trivial task is built from the product spec alone. tech_spec.md, once the investigator has proved the task can be built (from the repo's code and docs, a throwaway spike outside the repo only if needed): the parts of the change, the files each part owns, every name, interface and data shape between parts, and each id mapped to the part that delivers it. If the task cannot be built as asked it asks you; only when no answer can fix it, the run stops. Then docs_brief.md, for the docs ant, which cannot ask you anything: the purpose, readers, scope and non-goals, the reason behind each main design choice, and your answer for each root note and requirement file. Every docs question is asked while planning, inside the same 8. Last, one thin plan per worker ant: only that worker's slice of the specs, with its files, the spec ids it covers, the interfaces it uses, its tests and after; nothing is copied from the specs, which the worker reads for the detail. A run with one worker has no plan file: it builds straight from the specs. The plan script, which runs no ant, rejects bad or unknown ids, loops in after, two tasks on one file, paths outside the repo, a behaviour or invariant no plan covers, and a plan that covers none, before anything is built. Problems go back to the investigator once; still wrong, the run stops. Detectives check tasks against the plan and the tech spec; the judge scores the run against the product spec, id by id."},{"y":529.3,"sub":["one plan: one worker ant builds the whole task,","in its own worktree: code + tests + docs;","stuck: next fix round"],"name":"Worker ant","tip":"Build the plans, one worktree each.","src":"scripts/ishikari-build.js","id":"workers","code":"s6","x":1344.5,"about":"The main line: a run with one plan has one worker ant. It builds the whole task straight from the two specs, with no plan file, in its own git worktree. Two or more plans take the rail inside the ring, to the Worker ants. Writes code, tests and the docs its change affects, decides on its own and commits all its work. A worker that gets stuck says why, and that becomes a bug for the next fix round. A plan may name a saved workflow to run instead."},{"y":708.1,"sub":["checks the built task against plan + tech spec,","runs tests (reuses the worker's if clean);","finds each bug's cause and plans its fix"],"name":"Detective ant","tip":"Check each built task and plan every fix.","src":"skills/detective-ant/SKILL.md, scripts/ishikari-build.js","id":"detectives","code":"s7","x":1369.7,"about":"The main line: a run with one plan has one detective ant, started once the task is built. Two or more plans take the rail inside the ring, to the Detective ants. Loads the detective-ant skill in its Ishikari mode. Checks the work against its plan and the tech spec, and runs the tests. Each bug comes back with how to see it, its cause and a fix plan; a worker builds the fix and the detective re-checks. 3 tries per bug, 3 fix rounds, then the task drops. Never changes code. A dropped task's branch is kept for a later look, tasks built on it drop too, and the final report lists them."},{"y":876.4,"sub":["merges passing tasks in a scratch","copy, tests once: the combined test;","fewer than 2 passing tasks: no combined test"],"name":"Integrator ant","tip":"Merges all passing tasks in a scratch copy and tests once.","src":"scripts/ishikari-build.js (Combined phase)","id":"integrator","code":"s8","x":1335.5,"about":"Two tasks can pass alone and break together. It merges every passing task in a straight line in a throwaway copy and runs the tests once. A clashing task takes in the tasks it clashes with and goes back through the fix loop; 2 rounds. Skipped with fewer than 2 passing tasks."},{"y":1031.2,"sub":["merges in a straight line in a scratch copy,","or reuses build's trial merge; then checks","its own merge with git cherry"],"name":"Merger ant","tip":"Merges the approved tasks for real, then checks with git; failures go back to the workers.","src":"scripts/ishikari-finish.js (Merge phase)","id":"merger","code":"s9","x":1242.4,"about":"Adds every passing task's commits in a straight line, in dependency order, in a scratch copy, and tests once. It reuses build's trial merge when nothing moved. Then it checks its own merge with git cherry and counts changed lines with git diff --shortstat. Never touches main. A conflict, failed tests, or a task git finds missing goes back to the worker ant on its own branch: it merges the current main, fixes the bug, the detective re-checks, the integrator tests again, and finish retries the merge. Tasks that merged cleanly are not rebuilt. At most 2 extra build rounds; what is left drops and is reported."},{"y":1140.3,"sub":["cleans up dead code and mess itself: edits,","runs the tests, commits, lands it only if","they pass. The tech spec and the plans are not what it scores. The score is its own call, not an average. It lists every gap, and repeats as bugs the gaps where the code itself behaves wrongly; a missing or weak test is a gap, not a bug. Below 7 with gaps: one fix round for every gap, then a second score. 7 or more with bugs: the same round, for the bugs only. It changes only files under docs/ or doc/ and Markdown or Org files elsewhere, never code, tests or data, and never asks the user: open questions go in the docs' Open questions chapter. It runs docs/build.sh diagrams and check when present, then the tests, and fast-forwards the scratch copy only if all pass.
